extracted.intended_audience: patent owners, patent prosecutors, patent litigation attorneys, and third-party requesters
extracted.subtask_description: Overview of USPTO procedures, rights, timing, and effects for ex parte and inter partes reexamination of U.S. patents, including standards for granting/denying, prosecution steps, appeals, estoppel, and issuance of reexamination certificates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of a Pending Reexamination
rubrics_metrics.description: Each claim of a patent is presumed valid under 35 U.S.C. 282 and may be enforced notwithstanding the presence of a pending reexamination proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Litigation may move forward in parallel at the district court's discretion; results of reexamination may affect litigation. Under 35 U.S.C. 307, a patent is not revised by any amendment or cancellation of a claim made during reexamination until a reexamination certificate is issued. (Cites: Ethicon v. Quigg; Viskase; In re Etter)

rubrics_metrics.name: Ex Parte Reexamination — Who May Request and Basis
rubrics_metrics.description: A proceeding in which any person may request reexamination of a U.S. patent based on one or more prior patents or printed publications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A requester who is not the patent owner (a 'third party requester') has only limited participation rights in the proceeding. [MPEP 2209]

rubrics_metrics.name: Inter Partes Reexamination — Eligibility and Rights
rubrics_metrics.description: A proceeding in which any person who is not the patent owner and is not otherwise estopped may request reexamination of a U.S. patent issued from an original application filed on or after November 29, 1999 based on one or more prior patents or printed publications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Both patent owner and third party requester have participation rights throughout the proceeding, including appeal rights. [MPEP 2609]

rubrics_metrics.name: Reexamination Granted — Meaning of Grant
rubrics_metrics.description: An Order Granting Reexamination is not a determination of claim patentability; it indicates the request has established the existence of at least one Substantial New Question (SNQ) of patentability based upon prior patents and/or printed publications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing of Grant/Denial Mailing — Ex Parte
rubrics_metrics.description: In ex parte reexamination, the Order, whether granting or denying reexamination, must be mailed within three months of the filing date of the request for reexamination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: [MPEP 2241]

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing of Grant/Denial Mailing — Inter Partes
rubrics_metrics.description: In inter partes reexamination, the Order must be mailed not later than three months after the request is filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: [MPEP 2641]

rubrics_metrics.name: Reexamination Denied — Meaning of Denial
rubrics_metrics.description: An Order Denying Reexamination is not a determination of claim patentability; it is an order denying reexamination of any claims because the Office determined that no SNQ has been established in the request.

rubrics_metrics.name: Substantial New Question of Patentability (SNQ) Standard
rubrics_metrics.description: A request for reexamination must establish the existence of at least one new technological teaching affecting any claim of the patent that was not considered by the Office in a prior Office proceeding involving the patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The SNQ is established based on prior patents and/or printed publications. [MPEP 2242]

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice of Filing of Request for Reexamination
rubrics_metrics.description: Notice that a request for reexamination has been filed and accorded a filing date is published in the Official Gazette.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: [MPEP 2215]

rubrics_metrics.name: Rejection (Non-Final) — Initial Office Action
rubrics_metrics.description: The initial Office action on patentability (non-final rejection).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In ex parte reexamination the initial action is not mailed with the Order Granting Reexamination because patent owner may file optional comments, to which the third party requester may respond; the Office must await expiration of those periods before mailing the initial action. [MPEP 2262]

rubrics_metrics.name: Rejection (Non-Final) — Inter Partes Procedures for Initial Action
rubrics_metrics.description: In inter partes reexamination, the initial action may optionally be mailed together with the Order Granting Reexamination, but even if not, no party comments are permitted prior to the mailing of the initial action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Patent owner files a response to a non-final action that includes argument and/or evidentiary showing and/or amendments, and the response will be entered as a matter of right. Third party requester may thereafter respond with written comments directed to the Office action and to the patent owner’s response. [MPEP 2260]

rubrics_metrics.name: Rejection (Final) — Ex Parte Finality Consequences
rubrics_metrics.description: A second or subsequent action on patentability in an ex parte reexamination may be made 'final.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While responsive arguments may be considered, entry of an amendment or consideration of additional evidence is not a matter of right in a final rejection. Patent owner may appeal to the Board of Patent Appeals and Interferences (BPAI). [MPEP 2271]

rubrics_metrics.name: Action Closing Prosecution (ACP) — Inter Partes Finality Stage
rubrics_metrics.description: The second or subsequent action on patentability in an inter partes reexamination proceeding is called an Action Closing Prosecution (ACP).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Patent owner may respond with argument and/or evidentiary showing and/or amendments or choose not to respond. If patent owner files a response, then third party requester may file written comments directed only to the patent owner’s submission. Entry of the patent owner response is not a matter of right. Neither party may appeal at this point. [MPEP 2671.02]

rubrics_metrics.name: Right of Appeal Notice (RAN) — Trigger and Effect
rubrics_metrics.description: After considering any patent owner response to an ACP and any third party requester comments, or after expiration of the time to respond with no response, the examiner will either re-open prosecution or issue a Right of Appeal Notice (RAN).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The RAN sets time periods in which the parties may appeal to the BPAI, and the RAN closes prosecution. Any amendment filed after a RAN will not be entered. It is possible to issue a RAN after a patent owner response to the initial Office action if both parties stipulate the issues appropriate for a final rejection or final patentability determination. [MPEP 2673.02]

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeal to the BPAI — Ex Parte
rubrics_metrics.description: A notice of appeal is a proper response to a final rejection in an ex parte reexamination; only the patent owner may appeal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The appeal process is similar to that in a non-provisional patent application. [MPEP 2273]

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeal to the BPAI — Inter Partes
rubrics_metrics.description: Either party may file a notice of appeal as a proper response to a RAN in an inter partes reexamination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If some claims are rejected and some allowed or confirmed as patentable, both parties may appeal those determinations, file appeal briefs, respondent's briefs, and, after the examiner's answer, file rebuttal briefs directed to the examiner’s answer. [MPEP 2674]

rubrics_metrics.name: Subsequent (Court) Appeals — Ex Parte
rubrics_metrics.description: If the request for reexamination was filed prior to November 29, 1999, patent owner may appeal the decision of the BPAI to either the U.S. District Court for the District of Columbia or to the Court of Appeals for the Federal Circuit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the request was filed on or after November 29, 1999, patent owner may appeal only to the Federal Circuit. [MPEP 2279]

rubrics_metrics.name: Subsequent (Court) Appeals — Inter Partes
rubrics_metrics.description: Either party who was a party to an appeal to the BPAI and is dissatisfied with the result may appeal only to the Court of Appeals for the Federal Circuit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: [MPEP 2683]

rubrics_metrics.name: Concurrent Reexamination and Litigation — Expedited Handling
rubrics_metrics.description: If there is concurrent litigation and reexamination on a patent and the request for reexamination was filed as a result of court order, or the litigation has been stayed for the purpose of reexamination, the Office will expedite the proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expedition includes taking the case up for action at the earliest possible time, setting shorter response times, and permitting extensions of time only upon a strong showing of sufficient cause. [MPEP 2286]

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of Concluded Litigation on Reexamination — Validity Findings
rubrics_metrics.description: A court decision holding that a patent claim is valid will not preclude the Office from continuing to reexamine such claim in an ex parte reexamination proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Office applies the 'broadest reasonable interpretation' of claim language in reexamination because claims may be amended, whereas courts apply a less liberal standard; therefore the Office may find a claim unpatentable even if a court held it valid. [MPEP 2286]

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of Concluded Litigation on Reexamination — Invalidity Findings
rubrics_metrics.description: A final, non-appealable court decision holding that a patent claim is invalid will preclude the Office from ordering any reexamination proceeding for that claim or will result in termination of any previously ordered reexamination as to that claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: [MPEP 2286]

rubrics_metrics.name: Estoppel in Inter Partes Reexamination
rubrics_metrics.description: A final, nonappealable holding in litigation that a patent claim is valid may operate to estop a party from requesting inter partes reexamination of that claim or from maintaining a previously ordered inter partes reexamination of that claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Estoppel may also preclude a party who has obtained an Order Granting Inter Partes Reexamination from asserting invalidity of that claim in litigation under Section 1338 of Title 28 on grounds that such party raised, or could have raised, during that inter partes reexamination if that claim has been finally determined to be patentable in the inter partes reexamination proceeding. [MPEP 2686.04(V)]

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice of Intent to Issue Reexamination Certificate (NIRC)
rubrics_metrics.description: An NIRC is mailed to inform the parties that a reexamination proceeding has been terminated, whether by failure to timely file a required response or by natural resolution of all outstanding issues of claim patentability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The NIRC lists the status of all claims that were subject to reexamination, including canceled claims and any claims added during the proceeding that were determined to be patentable, and indicates which claims, if any, were not reexamined. An NIRC may include an examiner’s amendment and must include reasons for confirmation of any patent claims determined to be patentable without amendment, and reasons for allowance of any amended or newly added claims. [MPEP 2287]

rubrics_metrics.name: Reexamination Certificate — Conclusion of Proceeding
rubrics_metrics.description: A reexamination proceeding is concluded by publication of a reexamination certificate which amends the text of the patent that was reexamined.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The certificate is analogous to a certificate of correction and will contain the text of all changes to the patent that was the subject of the reexamination proceeding. [MPEP 2288 and 2290]

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice to the Public of Reexamination Certificate
rubrics_metrics.description: Publication of a reexamination certificate is announced in the Official Gazette.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: [MPEP 2691]
